original.title: Egg Drop Soup
original.description: A quick, silky chicken broth soup with delicate ribbons of egg, lightly thickened and seasoned with ginger and white pepper.
steps: Bring the chicken broth and ginger to a boil in a medium saucepan.
Stir in the soy sauce, sesame oil, white pepper, and salt.
Mix the cornstarch with the cold water until smooth, then stir it into the boiling broth and simmer for 1 minute until slightly thickened.
Beat the eggs well in a measuring cup with a spout.
Reduce the heat so the soup is barely simmering and stir it slowly in one direction to create a gentle whirlpool.
Pour the eggs in a thin, steady stream into the moving soup and let them set for 10 seconds before stirring gently to form ribbons.
Taste and adjust the salt, then ladle into bowls and garnish with green onions.

original.title: Beef and Broccoli
original.description: Tender velveted flank steak and crisp-tender broccoli tossed in a glossy garlic, ginger, and oyster sauce.
ingredients: 1 lb flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
steps: Toss the beef with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, and baking soda and let it marinate for 20 minutes.
Whisk the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.
Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain well.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Spread the beef in a single layer and sear for 1 minute without moving, then stir-fry for 1 minute until just browned; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the wok with the garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the broccoli and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the wok, stir the sauce, and pour it in.
Toss for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats everything, then drizzle with sesame oil and serve with rice.

original.title: Scallion Pancakes
original.description: Flaky, chewy pan-fried flatbreads layered with sesame oil and green onions, served with a soy dipping sauce.
steps: Place the flour in a bowl, pour in the boiling water while stirring with chopsticks, then add the cold water and mix into a shaggy dough.
Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for 5 minutes until smooth, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces and roll one piece into a thin 8-inch circle.
Brush the circle with sesame oil, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and a quarter of the green onions.
Roll the circle up tightly like a cigar, then coil the rope into a spiral and tuck the end underneath.
Flatten the spiral and gently roll it out into a 7-inch pancake; repeat with the remaining dough.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook a pancake for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Squeeze the hot pancake from the sides with two spatulas to fluff up the layers, then repeat with the rest.
Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and chili oil for dipping, cut the pancakes into wedges, and serve hot.

original.title: Dan Dan Noodles
original.description: Sichuan street noodles topped with crispy seasoned pork and a spicy, nutty sesame and chili oil sauce.
ingredients: 2 tbsp chopped Sichuan preserved vegetable (ya cai), optional
3 tbsp Chinese sesame paste or tahini
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry the pork for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and slightly crispy.
Add the Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and preserved vegetable and cook for 1 minute more, then set aside.
Whisk the sesame paste, soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, chili oil, Sichuan pepper, and garlic together in a bowl.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and blanch the bok choy for 1 minute, then remove.
Cook the noodles in the same water according to the package until just tender, reserving 1/4 cup of the cooking water.
Thin the sauce with the hot noodle water and divide it among four bowls.
Add the drained noodles and bok choy to the bowls and top with the pork, green onions, and peanuts.
Toss everything together at the table before eating.

original.title: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallion
original.description: A whole fish steamed until just tender, then finished with sizzling oil poured over fresh ginger and scallions and a light soy sauce.
ingredients: 1 (1 1/2 to 2 lb) whole sea bass, cleaned and scaled
2-inch piece fresh ginger, half sliced and half finely julienned
4 green onions, half cut into 3-inch pieces and half finely julienned
steps: Pat the fish dry, make two diagonal slashes on each side, and rub lightly with salt inside and out.
Lay the ginger slices and green onion pieces on a heatproof plate, place the fish on top, and drizzle with the Shaoxing wine.
Bring water to a boil in a wok or steamer large enough to hold the plate.
Steam the fish covered over high heat for 10 to 12 minutes until the flesh flakes easily at the thickest part near the bone.
Meanwhile, warm the light soy sauce, water, and sugar in a small saucepan until the sugar dissolves.
Carefully remove the plate, pour off the steaming liquid, and discard the cooked ginger and onion.
Scatter the julienned ginger and green onions over the fish.
Heat the oil in a small pan until it just begins to smoke, then pour it over the ginger and green onions so they sizzle.
Pour the warm soy mixture around the fish, garnish with cilantro, and serve immediately.

original.title: Hong Kong Egg Tarts
original.description: Buttery short-crust tart shells filled with a smooth, glossy, just-set egg custard, a dim sum bakery favorite.
steps: Whisk the flour, powdered sugar, and salt together, then rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Mix in the egg yolk and cold water until the dough just comes together, then wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Dissolve the sugar in the hot water and let it cool to room temperature.
Whisk the eggs gently with the evaporated milk and vanilla, stir in the cooled sugar syrup, and strain twice through a fine sieve.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and press each into a greased 3-inch tart tin or standard muffin cup, bringing it just above the rim.
Fill each shell about 90 percent full with custard.
Bake for 10 minutes, then reduce the oven to 350°F (175°C) and bake for 12 to 15 minutes more until the custard is set but still jiggles slightly.
Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then unmold and serve warm.

original.title: Wonton Soup
original.description: Plump pork and shrimp wontons in a clear, gingery chicken broth with baby bok choy.
ingredients: 4 oz shrimp, peeled, deveined, and finely chopped
steps: Combine the pork, shrimp, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, ginger, green onion, white pepper, and cornstarch and stir vigorously in one direction for 2 minutes until sticky.
Place 1 tsp filling in the center of a wrapper and moisten the edges with water.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle, press out the air and seal, then bring the two bottom corners together and pinch them to seal.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers, keeping the finished wontons covered with a damp towel.
Simmer the chicken broth with the ginger slices for 10 minutes, then remove the ginger and season with soy sauce and sesame oil.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook the wontons in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked through.
Add the bok choy to the broth and simmer for 2 minutes.
Divide the wontons and bok choy among bowls, ladle the hot broth over them, and garnish with green onions.

original.title: Sichuan Dry-Fried Green Beans
original.description: Green beans fried until blistered and wrinkled, then tossed with savory pork, garlic, and chilies.
ingredients: 1 lb green beans, trimmed and dried well
6 dried red chilies, snipped into pieces
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over medium-high heat and add the green beans.
Fry for 8 to 10 minutes, tossing occasionally, until the beans are blistered, wrinkled, and tender; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the wok and stir-fry the pork for 2 to 3 minutes until browned and crisp.
Add the dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant without burning.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 20 seconds.
Return the green beans to the wok and add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and salt.
Toss for 1 minute until everything is well coated, then serve hot.

original.title: Garlic Stir-Fried Bok Choy
original.description: Baby bok choy quickly stir-fried with plenty of garlic and a splash of soy for a fast, bright green side dish.
ingredients: 1 tbsp soy sauce or oyster sauce
steps: Halve the bok choy lengthwise, rinse well to remove grit, and shake dry.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering.
Add the garlic and stir-fry for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add the bok choy and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and water, cover, and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the stems are crisp-tender.
Drizzle with sesame oil, toss, and serve immediately.

original.title: Smashed Cucumber Salad
original.description: Crunchy smashed cucumbers dressed with garlic, black vinegar, soy, and chili oil, a refreshing cold dish.
steps: Lay a cucumber on a cutting board and smash it firmly along its length with the flat side of a cleaver or a rolling pin until it cracks open.
Cut the smashed cucumbers into bite-size pieces.
Toss the cucumbers with the salt and sugar in a colander and let drain for 10 minutes.
Stir together the garlic, black vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and chili oil.
Shake off the excess liquid from the cucumbers and toss them with the dressing.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and cilantro and serve right away, cold.

original.title: Orange Chicken
original.description: Crispy fried chicken pieces tossed in a sticky, sweet and tangy orange sauce, a Chinese-American takeout classic.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Toss the chicken with the egg and soy sauce.
Mix the cornstarch and flour in a bowl, then add the chicken and toss until each piece is well coated.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the chicken in batches for 5 to 6 minutes until golden, crisp, and cooked through, then drain on a wire rack.
Combine the orange juice, zest, sugar, rice vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, and red pepper flakes in a large skillet and bring to a boil.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer for 1 minute until thick and glossy.
Add the fried chicken to the sauce and toss until evenly coated.
Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds and serve with steamed rice.

original.title: Cumin Lamb Stir-Fry
original.description: Xinjiang-style lamb stir-fried with whole and ground cumin, dried chilies, and onions for a bold, smoky dish.
ingredients: 1 lb boneless lamb shoulder or leg, thinly sliced
steps: Toss the lamb with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch and marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat until it just begins to smoke.
Add the lamb in a single layer, sear for 1 minute, then stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes until browned; remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, the cumin seeds, ground cumin, red pepper flakes, dried chilies, and Sichuan pepper and stir-fry for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the onion and garlic and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the onion is just softened.
Return the lamb to the wok, sprinkle with salt and sugar, and toss for 1 minute.
Turn off the heat, toss in the cilantro, and serve with rice or flatbread.

original.title: Sesame Balls (Jian Dui)
original.description: Crisp, hollow glutinous rice balls coated in sesame seeds and filled with sweet red bean paste.
steps: Dissolve the brown sugar in the hot water.
Gradually stir the sugar water into the rice flour, then knead into a smooth, soft dough like play clay, adding a little more water or flour as needed.
Divide the dough into 16 pieces and the red bean paste into 16 small balls.
Flatten each piece of dough into a cup, place a ball of bean paste in the center, and pinch closed, rolling it into a smooth ball.
Dip each ball briefly in water and roll it in the sesame seeds, pressing gently so they stick.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 320°F (160°C).
Fry the balls in batches for 8 to 10 minutes, gently pressing them against the side of the pot with a ladle as they float so they puff and expand.
Remove when golden brown and drain on paper towels; serve warm.

original.title: Chinese Almond Cookies
original.description: Crumbly, buttery almond cookies topped with a whole almond, traditionally shared for good fortune at Lunar New Year.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
Whisk together the flour, almond flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt.
Beat the butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Beat in the egg yolk and almond extract.
Add the dry ingredients and mix on low until a soft dough forms.
Roll the dough into 1 1/4-inch balls, place them 2 inches apart on the sheets, and flatten slightly.
Press a whole almond into the center of each cookie and brush the tops with the lightly beaten egg white.
Bake for 13 to 15 minutes until the edges are lightly golden.
Cool on the sheets for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

original.title: Tangyuan (Sweet Rice Balls in Ginger Syrup)
original.description: Chewy glutinous rice dumplings filled with black sesame paste and served in a warm ginger syrup, eaten for family reunions.
ingredients: 3 tbsp unsalted butter or lard, softened
1/3 cup brown sugar or rock sugar
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant, then grind them finely with the sugar.
Mix the ground sesame with the softened butter into a paste, chill for 15 minutes, then roll into 16 small balls.
Gradually stir the warm water into the rice flour and knead into a smooth, soft dough.
Divide the dough into 16 pieces, flatten each into a cup, wrap around a sesame ball, and roll smooth.
Simmer the water, ginger, and brown sugar in a saucepan for 10 minutes to make the syrup.
Bring a separate pot of water to a boil and add the tangyuan, stirring gently so they don't stick.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until they float, then simmer 1 minute more.
Transfer the tangyuan to bowls and ladle the hot ginger syrup over them.

original.title: Hong Kong Milk Tea
original.description: Strong, smooth black tea brewed and pulled until silky, then mixed with evaporated and sweetened condensed milk.
ingredients: 2 tbsp sweetened condensed milk, or to taste
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a small saucepan.
Add the tea leaves, reduce the heat, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour the tea through a fine strainer or tea sock into a heatproof pitcher, then pour it back into the saucepan.
Repeat pouring the tea back and forth through the strainer 4 or 5 times to give it a smoother, richer body.
Simmer for 2 more minutes, then strain into two cups.
Stir in the evaporated milk and condensed milk and serve hot, or cool and pour over ice.

original.title: Lion's Head Meatballs
original.description: Large, tender pork meatballs braised with napa cabbage in a light soy broth, a classic Shanghai family dish.
ingredients: 1 lb napa cabbage, cut into large pieces
steps: Combine the pork, water chestnuts, green onions, ginger, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, salt, white pepper, egg, and cornstarch.
Stir vigorously in one direction for 3 to 4 minutes until the mixture is sticky and springy.
With wet hands, shape the mixture into 4 to 6 large meatballs, slapping them between your palms to compact them.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat and brown the meatballs on all sides for 6 to 8 minutes, turning gently; remove them.
Add the cabbage stems to the pot and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Lay the meatballs on the cabbage stems and cover them with the cabbage leaves.
Pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce, sugar, and ginger and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer gently for 40 to 45 minutes until the meatballs are very tender and cooked through.
Serve the meatballs in bowls with the cabbage and plenty of broth.
